meta.title: Linear Algebra Essentials
meta.subtitle: Vectors, inner products, matrices, and tensors

slides.title: Vectors and basis
body: A vector is an ordered list of numbers.
A basis is a set of vectors used to describe all others.
For qubits we use $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$ as the basis.
Why basis matters: the coordinates of a vector depend on which basis you choose.

slides.title: Linear combinations
body: Any vector is a weighted sum of basis vectors.
Example: $a|0\rangle + b|1\rangle$ is a linear combination.
Why this matters: superposition is just a linear combination with complex weights.

slides.title: Inner product
body: The inner product measures overlap between two vectors: $$\langle a|b\rangle = a^\dagger b$$
The norm is $\|v\| = \sqrt{\langle v|v\rangle}$.
Why conjugate: it makes lengths positive and keeps physics consistent with phases.

check.explain: Correct - orthonormal basis vectors have zero overlap.

slides.title: Bras, kets, conjugates
body: The conjugate transpose turns a ket into a bra.
If $|v\rangle = \begin{bmatrix}a\\b\end{bmatrix}$ then $\langle v| = [a^*, b^*]$.
Complex conjugation flips the sign of the imaginary part, which affects phase.

slides.title: Matrices as linear maps
body: A matrix maps vectors to vectors: $v \mapsto Mv$.
Example 2x2 matrix: $$M = \begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}$$
Why matrices: they describe how a gate acts on every basis vector at once.

quiz.question: If $M$ is 2x2 and $v$ is 2x1, what is the shape of $Mv$?
quiz.explain: A 2x2 matrix times a 2x1 vector yields a 2x1 vector.

slides.title: Matrix multiplication
body: Matrix multiplication composes linear maps.
Order matters: generally $AB \ne BA$.
Why this matters: the order of quantum gates changes the result.

slides.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
body: An eigenvector keeps its direction under $M$: $$Mv = \lambda v$$
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors describe the structure of $M$.
Why it matters: measurement outcomes correspond to eigenvalues of observables.

slides.title: Unitary matrices
body: Quantum gates must preserve norm.
A unitary matrix satisfies: $$U^\dagger U = I$$
Why unitary: it preserves inner products and keeps total probability equal to 1.

quiz.question: Which condition defines a unitary matrix?
quiz.explain: Unitarity means the conjugate transpose is the inverse.

slides.title: Hermitian observables
body: Hermitian matrices satisfy $A = A^\dagger$.
They have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors.
Why this matters: measurement results must be real numbers.

slides.title: Tensor products
body: Multi-qubit states use tensor products.
Example basis for two qubits: $|00\rangle$, $|01\rangle$, $|10\rangle$, $|11\rangle$.
$$|a\rangle \otimes |b\rangle$$
Why tensor products: they describe independent systems and scale the state space exponentially.
